evidence.note: Curled /api/health on all three nodes verifying node_id 0/1/2 — basic multi-node liveness check.
Registered on Node 0 and validated the bearer token on Node 1, an explicit cross-node persistence/auth check.
Created workspace on Node 1, posted a message on Node 2, read it back from Node 0 confirming seq:1 — a real cross-node dense-seq assertion.
Wrote a custom IRC client test script, posted via IRC, then confirmed via HTTP the message persisted and was sequenced next — a mixed web+IRC seq-density check (a level-8-style invariant).

Built a supervisor for auto-restart but never SIGKILL'd a node or the broadcaster to test resilience; no WS subscribe/resume/gap exercise and no UI selector verification, then deleted the test scripts (one-shot, not a repeatable harness).

reasoning: The agent ran the full three-node cluster and exercised representative HTTP flows plus a custom IRC driver, checking cross-node auth and a mixed web+IRC dense-seq invariant — clearly above the level-5 anchor and touching a level-8 element (cross-protocol seq density). But it never exercised WebSockets (no subscribe/resume/gap), never actually SIGKILL'd a node or the broadcaster to confirm survival within the 5s bound, and never verified UI selectors, so it falls short of the layered kill-and-recover harness the level-8/10 anchors describe. This places it at a 6, between the basic cross-node checks of 5 and the failure-injection harness of 8.
